name: stale-approval
defect: APP-100 was approved at 09:00Z. Two commits landed on its branch at 11:20Z and 11:44Z, one of them changing the rounding mode the reviewer signed off. The ledger still shows one approval, and the row still says done.
why: board-doctor checks that an approval EXISTS and that it did not come from the owner. It does not compare the approval's timestamp against the code it approved — that part of the original note still stands, and board-doctor is still not the right layer to ask.
gap: STALE NARRATIVE, CORRECTED 2026-08-04. This entry used to claim the input was structurally missing: 'until an approval names a commit, approved is a claim about a moment, not about a diff'. That has been false since 2026-07-31. `board.mjs move ... approved --bind` computes `commit` and `diff_hash` from git and records them on the event; `scripts/approval-check.mjs` recomputes and verifies them, and as of 2026-08-04 `ship-gate.sh` finally passes it `--head` so the comparison actually runs at release time. The detector exists. What is still missing is THIS FIXTURE: it carries a docs/ tree with no bound approval and no git history, so there is nothing for approval-check to be pointed at — hence `expected_detector: null`, and hence this project stays OUT of the scored denominator rather than being counted as a caught defect it did not catch. Rebuilding the fixture as a real repo with a bound approval and a later commit is tracked work, not an unknown. Flagged by the 2026-08-03 post-enhancement audit (F-08) as a manifest whose narrative outlived the code it describes, which is why the lifecycle fields above now exist: `status` and `fixed_in` make this contradiction visible instead of leaving it to be re-discovered by the next reader.
